title: XMM and Einstein Probe retain a finite ASASSN-14ko decay mismatch under broad rate bounds
abstract: We extend an interval-set test of the ASASSN-14ko X-ray clock with XMM-Newton cycle 30 and Einstein Probe cycle 34. The test assigns no event-time probability within visit gaps. The earlier Swift and NICER set permits the published decay when suppression levels vary from 20 to 60 percent and rates move by two reported error units. With XMM and Einstein Probe, this decay needs maximum absolute event-time shifts of at least 1.799 days after a free phase and period fit. A further 20-percent baseline allowance reduces the bound to 1.353 days. Three epochs give an algebraic proof, and a ten-cycle witness attains the bound. An exact constant-dP/dt clock gives 1.349 days. A constant clock is feasible without added shifts in every test. The broadest bound is unchanged in three tested XMM bands. Independent one-day marker offsets for the two added instruments leave a 0.495-day mismatch; two-day offsets can remove it. These are conditional deterministic bounds, not confidence limits. They strengthen the timing evidence without proving a stellar orbital stall or excluding a shared debris-return delay. We supply code, input hashes, interval sets, fit witnesses, proof checks and retrieval instructions. External visit tables remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Feasible curvature extrema for independent suppression levels from 20 to 60 percent. Adding Einstein Probe and replacing cycle 30 with XMM remove the published local decay from the zero-shift set under the tested rate bounds. These are deterministic sets, not confidence limits.
